title: Proactive synthetic-degradation harness for multi-region GPU pressure and dependency sensitivity testing
creator: Marcus Li
description: Background: We need a controlled, reproducible harness that can synthesize realistic degradation patterns across heterogeneous infra slices (regional, GPU-pool-level, and dependent-service failures) so we can calibrate SLO alerting, exercise circuit-breakers/load-shedding policies, and produce operational runbooks. Goal: build an experiment harness that can trigger: (1) gradual GPU-pool exhaustion (queue growth + OOM-like rejection), (2) regional network partition/egress degradation with asymmetric latency, and (3) dependency failure modes (cascading timeouts / synthetic blackhole responses) against staging and pre-prod. The harness should be tenant-aware (canary-only by default), safe to abort, and integrate with existing observability (console dashboards, per-route token-level tracing). This ticket covers design, implementation of the harness primitives, baseline SLO experiments, and a short follow-up that recommends tuned circuit-breaker thresholds and load-shed policies.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run three canonical scenarios independently and in combination: region-egress-degradation, gpu-pool-pressure, dependency-silence
Canary routing is enforced so only tagged internal tenants receive synthetic traffic (no customer routing)
Circuit-breaker and load-shed behaviors are observable and reproducible; thresholds trip within expected percentiles documented in experiment runbook
SLO alerting rules (latency P95/P99 and error rate) produce signals consistent with injected degradation for at least two model routes
No uncontrolled customer-facing outages in staging/pre-prod; abort path verified and <1 minute to stop all synthetic traffic
Artifacts created: experiment notebook, results dashboard, PR with harness code, and a short runbook with recommended threshold changes
testing_plan: Phase 0: Small dry-run in isolated dev cluster to validate tooling and safety gates
Phase 1: Staging single-region gpu-pressure sweep (low->high queue length) while monitoring per-tenant latency and admission metrics
Phase 2: Staging region-egress degradation (increase tail latency and packet loss) to verify smart-routing fallback and cross-region failover behavior
Phase 3: Dependency fault injection: inject silent responses and intermittent 5xx from a critical downstream (routing/kv) to validate circuit-breakers and client backoff
Phase 4: Combined stress: overlap GPU pressure with dep-failure to observe emergent behaviors and priority-driven tenant fairness
Each phase includes gated rollout, canary validation, and post-run automated metrics collection (p95/p99, error-rate, admission-drop-rate, cached-hit-rate)
safety_controls: Default run mode: canary-only internal tenants (hard-coded token allowlist), environment flag required to run in broader staging
Global kill-switch API that stops generators and clears canary traffic tokens; documented and smoke-tested before Phase 1
Rate caps on synthetic traffic so aggregate load cannot exceed 15% of cluster headroom
Automated check that runtime autoscaling is enabled and GPU pool drain time > configured threshold before running pressure experiments
Experiment owner required to be on-call SRE during runs and escalation channel pre-notified
monitoring_queries: console:kv_latency_p99{env=staging,service=KV} spikes correlated with injected dep fault
console:tenant_error_rate{tenant=canary} remains within expected bounds for controlled experiments
updates: 2025-02-11: Kickoff sync with SRE, Runtime, and PM. Agreed on 3 canonical scenarios and safety gates. Action: runtime to expose pool-level admission metrics (owner: Tara Nguyen).
2025-02-12: Design review complete. Decided to implement pressure generator as traffic-replay + synthetic tokens rather than load-testing arbitrary clients to maintain realism of request patterns.
2025-02-14: Runtime PR created to add 'admission_queue_length' metric and a 'simulate-gpu-pressure' flag to local dev runtime (PR #137). Linked in artifacts.
2025-02-16: Implemented kill-switch endpoint and allowlist enforcement. Verified abort time of synthetic traffic = 18 seconds in dev. Added tests to harness repo.

2025-02-17: Staging Phase 1 run executed (single-region GPU pressure). Observations: p95 latency rose 42% for the synthetic canary route, circuit-breaker on that client tripped at 12s timeout as expected. Two follow-ups: (1) reduce synthetic token rate by 10% next run to avoid saturating autoscaler warm-up window; (2) add short delay before pressure ramp to ensure KV cache warmup completes.
2025-02-18: Preparing Phase 2 (region-egress). Notified customer-facing teams of staging run window. Next: collect full trace samples and runbook draft for SLO threshold recommendations.
